ing: divided, plus more for the water
st: Rinse the rice in cold water until it runs clear. Soak it in warm salted water for [[30 minutes]], then drain.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] of the butter in a pot over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb cubes for 8 minutes, then add the onion and cook 5 more minutes.
Add the water, [[1 tsp]] salt, and pepper. Cover and simmer for 45 minutes until the lamb is tender. Stir in the apricots, raisins, and chestnuts for the last 10 minutes.
Boil the drained rice in a big pot of salted water for 5 minutes until just par-cooked, then drain.
Steep the saffron in 3 tablespoons hot water. Mix a few spoonfuls of the drained rice with the saffron water to color it.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a wide heavy pot. Spread half the rice in the bottom, then top with the lamb and fruit with a little of its juices.
Cover with the rest of the white rice, then scatter the saffron rice on top. Dot with the last [[2 tbsp]] butter.
Poke a few steam holes with a spoon handle, wrap the lid in a clean towel, and cover tightly.
Cook on the lowest heat for 30 minutes, until the rice is fluffy and a golden crust has formed on the bottom. Serve with the lamb and fruit on top.
If using jarred leaves, rinse them well in cold water and drain. Trim off any tough stems.
Mix the ground lamb, rinsed rice, onions, mint, cilantro, salt, and pepper in a bowl until well combined.
Lay a leaf shiny side down with the stem end toward you. Place about 1 tablespoon of filling near the stem.
Fold in the sides, then roll up tightly into a small cigar shape. Repeat with remaining leaves.
Line the bottom of a wide pot with a few spare leaves. Pack the dolma in tight layers, seam side down.
Pour the melted butter and hot water over the dolma. Set a heavy plate on top so they do not unroll.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 50 minutes. The lamb must reach 160°F (71°C) and the rice should be tender.
Let rest for [[10 minutes]], then serve warm with the yogurt on the side.
Mix the flour, egg, warm water, and [[0.5 tsp]] salt into a stiff dough. Knead for 8 minutes, wrap, and rest for [[30 minutes]].
Mix the ground lamb, grated onion, fresh mint, and [[0.5 tsp]] salt for the filling.
Roll the dough very thin and cut into small squares about 1 inch across.
Put a tiny bit of filling, about 1/4 teaspoon, in the middle of each square. Fold into a triangle, then pinch the corners together into a little hat.
Bring the broth to a simmer with the remaining [[0.5 tsp]] salt.
Add the dumplings in batches and simmer 10 to 12 minutes, until they float and the lamb is cooked through to 160°F (71°C).
Mix the garlic and vinegar together in a small bowl.
Ladle the dumplings and broth into bowls. Add some garlic vinegar and a pinch of dried mint to each.

ing: cut into chunks, with some fat
st: Soak the dried chickpeas in water overnight, then drain and rinse.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Divide the lamb, chickpeas, and onions among 4 oven-safe bowls or a single heavy casserole.
Add the salt, pepper, and turmeric. Pour in the water, dividing it among the bowls so everything is just covered.
Cover tightly with foil and bake for 1 hour 30 minutes.
Add the potatoes, chestnuts, and plums. Re-cover and bake 45 more minutes, until the chickpeas and lamb are very tender.
Stir in the saffron water and bake another 15 minutes.
Drain the broth into a bowl and serve it first with bread. Then mash the meat and vegetables with a fork and serve them on a plate.

ing: with plenty of fat, about 20 percent
st: Squeeze the grated onion in a towel to remove as much liquid as you can.
Mix the lamb, onion, salt, and pepper in a bowl. Knead firmly with your hands for 5 minutes until the mixture becomes sticky and paste-like.
Cover and refrigerate for [[30 minutes]] so the meat firms up and is easier to shape.
Heat a grill to medium-high. Wet your hands and press a handful of meat around a flat metal skewer into a 6-inch sausage shape.
Grill the kebabs for 8 to 10 minutes, turning often, until browned and cooked through to 160°F (71°C).
Grill the tomato halves cut side down for 4 minutes until charred.
Warm the lavash on the grill for 30 seconds.
Slide the kebabs off the skewers onto the bread. Dust with sumac and serve with tomatoes and sliced onion.
Mix the flour, warm water, and [[1 tsp]] salt into a soft dough. Knead 5 minutes, cover, and rest for [[30 minutes]].
For the filling, toss the chopped spinach, dill, cilantro, and green onions with the remaining [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Squeeze out any liquid.
Divide the dough into 8 pieces and roll each into a very thin circle about 8 inches wide.
Spoon some of the greens over half of each circle and fold the other half over to make a half moon. Press the edges to seal.
Heat a dry skillet or griddle over medium heat.
Cook each qutab for 1 to 2 minutes per side, until brown spots appear and the dough looks dry.
Brush each hot qutab with melted butter right away.
Serve warm with yogurt on the side.
Whisk the yogurt, egg, and flour in a large pot until completely smooth. This stops the yogurt from curdling.
Stir in the water and set the pot over medium heat.
Stir constantly in one direction as it warms. Do not let it boil hard.
When it begins to bubble gently, add the rinsed rice and lower the heat. Simmer 15 minutes, stirring often.
Add the spinach, green onions, and salt. Cook for another 10 minutes until the rice is tender.
Stir in the dill, cilantro, and fresh mint and cook for 3 minutes.
Taste and add salt, then ladle into bowls and sprinkle with dried mint. Serve hot, or chilled in summer.
Salt the eggplant chunks lightly and let them sit in a colander for [[15 minutes]]. Pat dry.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large heavy skillet (or a wok) over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb cubes for 8 minutes.
Add the onions and cook 4 minutes until soft.
Move the meat to the side and add the potatoes. Fry for 10 minutes, turning, until browned at the edges.
Add the remaining oil, the eggplant, and bell peppers. Cook 8 minutes, stirring.
Add the tomatoes, salt, and pepper. Cover and cook on medium-low heat for 15 minutes, until the lamb is tender and the potatoes are soft.
Sprinkle with cilantro and serve hot, straight from the pan, with bread.

ing: melted and clarified if you like
st: Mix the flour, egg yolks, [[0.25 cup]] of the melted butter, and warm milk into a smooth dough. Knead 5 minutes and rest for [[30 minutes]].
Mix the walnuts with [[0.5 cup]] of the sugar and the cardamom.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Roll out the dough in thin sheets (about 8 sheets) to fit a 9 by 13 inch pan.
Brush the pan with butter. Layer 4 dough sheets, brushing each with butter, then spread the walnut mixture over.
Top with the last 4 buttered sheets. Cut diamond shapes through all the layers and pour the remaining butter over the top.
Bake for 45 minutes until deep golden and crisp.
Meanwhile, simmer the remaining [[0.5 cup]] sugar, water, honey, and saffron for 10 minutes. Stir in the lemon juice.
Pour the cooled syrup over the hot pakhlava. Let it soak for at least [[2 hours]] before serving.

ing: one for the dough, one for brushing
st: Mix the flour and baking powder, then rub in the butter. Add the egg, one yolk, and the warm milk. Knead into a soft dough.
Cover the dough and rest for [[30 minutes]].
Mix the ground almonds, sugar, and cardamom for the filling.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C). Roll the dough 1/8 inch thick and cut 3-inch circles.
Put a spoonful of filling on each circle, fold in half, and pinch the edges.
Crimp the edges with a fork or pleat them with pinched fingers to make a crescent.
Place on a lined baking sheet and brush with the remaining beaten yolk.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden. Cool on the pan for 10 minutes.
